To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a direct and simple derivatization of free fatty acids in human plasma was investigated for gas chromatographic analysis.
a new method has been developed to determine concentration and isotopic composition of FFAs in plasma.
the direct method of analysis for FFAs is more accurate and precise than a conventional method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the direct determination of FFAs in plasma.
the development of a new and simple method for the determination and analysis of free fatty acid concentration in plasma.
the determination of the concentrations and isotopic enrichments of plasma FFAs using a direct method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the direct derivatization method using dimethylamine and Deoxo-Flor is a simple and accurate method for determination of FFAs in plasma, and that it is suitable for the analysis of isotopic enrichment in plasma FFAs.
direct derivatization is superior to TLC separation and BF(3)/methanol derivatization for both FFA concentration and [(13)C]-FFA enrichment determination.
the new method is superior in terms of accuracy and precision for both concentration and enrichment measurements of FFAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this direct GC-FID method is a good alternative to the conventional BF(3)/Methanol-TLC GC-FID method for the measurement of FFAs in plasma.
direct derivatization with dimethylamine and Deoxo-Fluror is a very useful tool in the measurement of FFAs, especially when coupled with GC-C-IRMAS.
direct derivatization of FFAs to dimethylamides is a very simple, direct and efficient method for the determination and quantitation of concentration and enrichment in human plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the direct method is more accurate than the BF(3)-TLC method for the determination and measurement of [(13)C]-FFA enrichment and concentration.
the direct derivatization method provides more reliable results in terms of concentration and enrichment than does the BF(3) method.
the direct dimethyl derivative method is simple, rapid, accurate, precise and efficient and can be easily implemented in clinical studies.
